2C.3 The fear of God must be constantly maintained.
14A.1 Whatever animals that have divided or cloven hoofs and chews its cud you may eat.
14A.2 Fishes that have fins and scales may be eaten (Bass, croppie, flounder, cod, haddock, pike, salmon, sunfish, mackerel, snapper, trout, perch, smelt, tuna, etc.).
14A.3 All clean birds can be eaten (e.g., chicken, turkey, pheasant, quail, grouse, partridge, etc.).
14A.6 Animals which you can eat--ox, sheep, goats, deer, roebuck, gazelle, fallow deer, wild goat, antelope, buffalo, caribou, elk, ibex, wild ox, moose, chamois.
14B.1 Camel (does not have a divided hoof).
14B.2 Rabbits, hares, and rock hyrax (does not have a divided hoof).
14B.3 Cattle which either do not chew the cud or divide the hoof (horse, donkey, quagga, llama, etc.).
14B.4 Swine or hog (does not chew the cud).
14B.6 All water life that does not have fins and scales are not to be eaten (e.g., shrimp, lobster, snails, clams, shark, shell fish, eels, catfish, scallop, octopus, etc.).
14B.7 Every creeping thing that flies is unclean.

14B.8 Unclean birds-Eagle, buzzard, osprey, vultures, kite, ravens, owl, night hawk, ostrich, hawk, little owl, cormorant, great owl, falcon, swan, pelican, stork, herons, hoopoe, bats (and the eggs of unclean birds).
14D.1 You shall not eat anything which dies of itself.
14D.2 That which dies of itself may be given or sold to foreigners.
14D.5 You shall not eat any abominable thing.
14D.7 You are not to boil a kid in the milk of its mother.
14F.1 You are not to disfigure your body by making any cuttings in your flesh or tattoo marks in your skin.
15C.1 We should be of aid and help to the fatherless and widows with their afflictions.
15E.2 At the end of three years all of the tithes of the people's increase for the year are to be gathered together and given to and eaten by the stranger, the fatherless and the widow.
20E.6 A tenth of all the produce of the land is to be tithed to God.
20E.10 Tithes of food and first fruits of the land are to be eaten by all the people, the foreigners, and the poor as a feast to God.
